items.title: Why your voice sounds weird on recordings
items.summary: Why your voice sounds weird on recordings. When you talk, sound reaches your ear through the air and through your skull. Bone carries frequencies up to about 1 kHz, so you sound deeper to yourself. A microphone only hears the air path. Source: JAIST (Unoki), Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 2021. Idea: ASAP SCIENCE. Clips: Daniel Thrasher, "When you hear your own voice for the first time" (YouTube); Pixabay footage by Engin_Akyurt, stevediaz, MrWashingt0n, intersubjektiv, magicmore, NeuroPixels, VFS_World, Bastien86, flutie8211, iwsky, conte_public, mephala1980. Do you hate your recorded voice? So send this to the friend who refuses to listen to their own voice notes. #Shorts #voice #science #sound

items.title: Quoting Scott Aaronson
items.summary: It’s now obvious that we’ll be getting, not one-off solutions to this or that complexity question, but a whole new continent of mathematical truth, one that we’d previously only glimpsed through fog. Picture van Leeuwenhoek first training a microscope on pondwater, or Galileo first training his telescope on the stars. That might give you some idea of how our resolution into the complexity-theoretic universe, and the whole universe of mathematical truth beyond it, has now improved. — Scott Aaronson Tags: mathematics , llms , ai , generative-ai

items.title: Why airplane windows have a tiny hole
items.summary: Why airplane windows have a tiny hole. Cruise altitude air is about 3.4 psi and the cabin is about 11, so each window is pushed outward with roughly 8 psi. The hole in the middle pane lets cabin air reach the outer pane, which carries the load. Sources: ScienceAlert (GKN Aerospace, American Vacuum Society), FAA 14 CFR 25.841. items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.summary: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass.
